record.title: The generalized Hodge conjecture
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety. Define the coniveau filtration by

$$
N^iH^m(X)=\bigcup_{\operatorname{codim} Z\geq i}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(H^m_Z(X)\otimes\mathbb{Q}\longrightarrow H^m(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}\bigr),
$$

where $Z\subset X$ ranges over subvarieties, and let $H^{m,i}_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)$ be the largest Hodge substructure of $F^iH^m(X)_{\mathbb{C}}\cap H^m(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$. **The generalized Hodge conjecture.** For all $m$ and $i$, one has

$$
H^{m,i}_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)=N^iH^m(X).
$$

This extends the classical Hodge conjecture from algebraic classes in even-degree cohomology to the entire cohomology. The source presents it as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Stein's path-orientation conjecture for oriented graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be an oriented graph, and let $4\delta^0(G)4$ denote its minimum semidegree, the minimum of the in-degree and out-degree over all vertices. An **oriented path of length** $\ell$ is an orientation of a path with $\ell$ edges. **Stein's conjecture.** Every oriented graph $G$ contains all oriented paths of length $2\delta^0(G)-1$. The bound is best possible by considering disjoint unions of regular tournaments on $2\delta^0(G)-1$ vertices. The conjecture is supported by several partial results, including the directed-path case and cases with one change in direction, but its arbitrary-orientation case is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Completeness conjecture for weighted extremal families in the Erdős–Kleitman problem
record.statement:
Write $n=sm+c=s(m+1)-\ell$, and for $0\le k\le m$ define

$$
\mathcal H^k(m,s,\ell)=\{F\subseteq[n]\colon k|F|+|F\cap[a_k]|\ge m(k+1)\},\qquad a_k=ms-kc-1,
$$

and let $\mathcal P(m,s,\ell)$ be the shifted family $\{F\subseteq[n]\colon |F|+|F\cap[\ell-1]|\ge m+1\}$. **Completeness conjecture.** For every $n$ and $s$ with $n=sm+c=s(m+1)-\ell$,

$$
e(n,s)=\max\left\{|\mathcal H^0(m,s,\ell)|,|\mathcal H^1(m,s,\ell)|,\ldots,|\mathcal H^m(m,s,\ell)|,|\mathcal P(m,s,\ell)|\right\}.
$$

Moreover, every extremal family is isomorphic to one of the candidates attaining this maximum. The conjecture proposes that these known weighted constructions form a complete list of extremal families; the source does not give a resolution.

record.title: The ideal-prime conjecture for convexity
record.statement:
A **6-net** is a simplicial triangulation of the $2$-sphere with maximum degree at most $6$. A net is **prime** if every $3$-cycle bounds a face. An **ideal neoplatonic** is an equilateral ideal hyperbolic polyhedron, and $\Delta(\sigma,\infty)$ denotes the ideal neoplatonic realization associated to a $6$-net $\sigma$.

**Ideal-prime conjecture.** If the $6$-net $\sigma$ is prime, its ideal neoplatonic realization $\Delta(\sigma,\infty)$ is convex.

The source proves this assertion for prime $6$-nets with $v\leq50$, including uniqueness of the convex realization. Its validity for arbitrary prime $6$-nets remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Fajtlowicz's conjecture on average neighbour degree and distance spectra
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple connected graph of order $n=|V(G)|\ge2$. For each vertex $v$, let $d(v)$ be its degree and $N(v)$ its open neighbourhood, and define

$$
d^*(v)=\frac1{d(v)}\sum_{u\in N(v)}d(u),\qquad \delta^*(G)=\min_{v\in V(G)}d^*(v).
$$

Let $D(G)$ be the distance matrix of $G$, and write $\lambda_{\min}(D(G))$ for its smallest eigenvalue. **Fajtlowicz's conjecture.** If $G$ has order at least three and girth at least five, then

$$
\delta^*(G)\le-\lambda_{\min}(D(G)).
$$

This is a Graffiti conjecture attributed to Fajtlowicz's 1998 *Written on the Wall* report and recorded by Aouchiche and Hansen. Its resolution is not established by the supplied text.

record.title: The symmetric Pisier estimate for the $ ell$-functional
record.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ be an origin-symmetric convex body, let $GL_n$ denote the group of invertible linear transformations of $\mathbb R^n$, and let $\ell(K)$ be the product functional discussed in the paper. **Symmetric Pisier estimate.** There exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that, for every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, one can find $T\in GL_n$ satisfying

$$
\ell(TK)\leq C\sqrt{\log n}.
$$

The estimate would improve the general affine bound of order $\log n$ for origin-symmetric convex bodies; the supplied text presents it as believed rather than established, so its resolution remains open.

record.title: Erdős–Sós order-form conjecture for bipartite host graphs
record.statement:
Every tree is bipartite. Write $T_{a,b}=(A,B)$ when the two parts of $T$ satisfy

$$
|A|=a,\qquad |B|=b,\qquad a\geq b.
$$

For a bipartite graph $H$, let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathrm{bip}}(N;H)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free bipartite graph on $N$ vertices. **Order-form conjecture.** For every tree $T_{a,b}$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathrm{bip}}(N;T_{a,b})\leq\begin{cases} \frac12(a-1)N& \text{if}\ a\geq2b-1,\\ (b-1)N& \text{if}\ a\leq2b-1. \end{cases}
$$

The claim is motivated by two natural lower-bound constructions, whose comparison suggests a transition at $a=2b-1$. Its resolution is not supplied in the source material.

record.title: Erdős–Sós fixed-part conjecture for bipartite host graphs
record.statement:
Let $T_{a,b}=(A,B)$ be a tree whose bipartition satisfies

$$
|A|=a,\qquad |B|=b,\qquad a\geq b.
$$

For a bipartite graph $H$, let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathrm{bip}}(m,n;H)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free bipartite graph with part-sizes $m$ and $n$. **Fixed-part conjecture.** For every tree $T_{a,b}$ and all $m\geq b-1$, $n\geq a-1$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathrm{bip}}(m,n;T_{a,b})\leq(b-1)n+\begin{cases} (a-b)m&\text{if}\ a\geq2b-1,\\ (b-1)m&\text{if}\ a\leq2b-1. \end{cases}
$$

This refines the order-form problem by prescribing both part-sizes. The source motivates it through lower-bound constructions, but provides no resolution status for the conjecture.

record.title: Cylindrical-strip Beraha-zero pattern conjecture
record.statement:
Let $L$ be the width of a triangular-lattice strip with cylindrical boundary conditions, let $B_k$ denote the Beraha numbers, and let $D(q)$ be the amplitude matrix. **Cylindrical-strip Beraha-zero pattern conjecture.** The Beraha numbers where $\det D(q)$ vanishes are given by the union of the sets

$$
\{B_2,B_3,\ldots,B_{L+1}\}\quad\text{and}\quad\{B_{4k-2}\mid k=1,2,\ldots,\lfloor L/2\rfloor\}.
$$

The upper limit on $k$ is the integer part of $L/2$. This conjecture is based on systematic checks through $B_{50}$ and the observed cylindrical-boundary examples; unlike the free and zig-zag cases, the cylindrical data exhibit additional zeros beyond $B_{L+1}$, and the proposed general pattern remains open.

record.statement: Let $q_0(L)$ denote the maximum real value in the limiting curve for a square-lattice strip of width $L$ with fully periodic boundary conditions. **Odd-width square-lattice conjecture.** For widths $L=2p+1$ with $p\geq 1$, one has $q_0(L)=3$. record.title: Triangular-lattice q2 convergence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $q_2(L)$ denote the crossing of the two largest eigenvalues in the $\ell=2$ sector for a triangular-lattice strip of width $L$ with fully periodic boundary conditions, and let $q_{\rm B}\simeq3.8196717312$ be Baxter's equimodularity value. **Triangular-lattice $q_2$ convergence conjecture.** The limit

$$
q_2(\mathrm{tri})=\lim_{L\to\infty}q_2(L)
$$

exists and equals $q_{\rm B}$; moreover, $q_2(3p)$ is monotonically decreasing in $p$. Numerical fits support the claim and imply a common limiting value with $q_0(\mathrm{tri})$, but no proof is given.

record.title: Existence of superregular matrices over fields of size $2^{\gamma-2}$
record.statement:
Let $b3\geq 5$. A $b3\times b3$ matrix over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{2^{\gamma-2}}$ is **superregular** if every nontrivial minor is nonzero.

**Superregular matrix existence conjecture.** For every integer $b3\geq 5$, there exists a $b3\times b3$ superregular matrix over

$$
\mathbb{F}_{2^{\gamma-2}}.
$$

The conjecture would significantly improve the general upper bound on the field size required for constructing superregular matrices, which in turn are used to construct convolutional codes with a maximum distance profile. The paper presents it based on computer searches; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Fekete's aperture-angle approximation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $C$ be a compact convex figure in the plane, let $\alpha(C,k)$ denote the best worst-case aperture-angle approximation of $C$ by an inscribed convex $k$-gon, and let $\alpha(k)=\inf_C\alpha(C,k)$. A regular $(k+1)$-gon has interior angle $\bigl(1-\frac{2}{k+1}\bigr)\pi$. **Fekete's conjecture.** For any $k\geq 2$, the smallest value of $\alpha(k)$ is achieved by the regular $(k+1)$-gon, and therefore

$$
\alpha(k)=\bigl(1-\frac{2}{k+1}\bigr)\pi.
$$

The conjecture was known for $k=2$ and $k=3$ and was supported by experiments; the paper proves it, first for polygons and then for arbitrary compact convex sets by a limit argument.

record.title: Bray's multiple-end Penrose conjecture
record.statement:
Let $(M^3,g,h)$ be complete, asymptotically flat Cauchy data with $\mu \ge |J|$ and more than one end. Choose one end as special, and let $A$ be the minimum area required to enclose all the other ends. Let $m$ be the total mass of the chosen end. **Bray's multiple-end Penrose conjecture.** Then

$$
m \ge \sqrt{A/16\pi}.
$$

This formulation uses trapped surfaces in the nonspecial ends to motivate an event horizon enclosing those ends. The supplied text does not establish whether the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Closed-boundary rotor-model groundstate sum conjecture
record.statement:
For the rotor model with closed boundary conditions, let $\psi_0$ be its groundstate wavefunction and let $S(N)$ denote the sum of its elements. For odd size $N=2m-1$, normalize the smallest element to $A_{\rm V}(2m-1;3)$. $$
S(2m-1)=3^{(m-1)^2}N_8(2m).
$$

For even sizes,

$$
S(2m)=3^{2\theta_m}A_{\rm V}(2m+1),

$$
\theta_m=\left\lfloor\frac{(m-1)(m+2)}{3}\right\rfloor,

record.title: The fewnomial bound for non-degenerate positive roots
record.statement:
Let $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ be an $n\times n$ fewnomial system over $\mathbb{R}$ of type $(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$, where each $f_i$ is an $n$-variate $m_i$-nomial in real monomials. A root is non-degenerate when the Jacobian of $F$ at that root has full rank, and the positive orthant is $\mathbb{R}^n_+=\\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:x_i>0\text{ for all }i\\}$.

**Fewnomial root-count conjecture.** The maximum number of non-degenerate roots of $F$ in the positive orthant is

$$
\prod_{i=1}^n(m_i-1).
$$

This is presented as a multivariate generalization of the sharp $m-1$ bound from Descartes' Rule of Signs for a univariate polynomial with $m$ monomial terms. The source gives no resolution status for this bound.

record.title: Conjecture on sublinear chromatic-root bounds for series-parallel graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite undirected graph, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, and let $\pi(G,z)$ be its chromatic polynomial.

**Series-parallel chromatic-root bound.** There exists a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every series-parallel graph $G$ of maximum degree $k$, every chromatic root $z$ lies in

$$
|z-1|\leq C\,\frac{k}{\log k}.
$$

The paper proves a bound of this order for generalized theta graphs and conjectures that the methods extend to arbitrary series-parallel graphs; it also remarks that an analogous statement for all planar graphs is only conceivable, not asserted.

record.title: Maxmaxflow conjecture for bounded chromatic roots
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, define the edge-connectivity between distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ by

$$
\lambda(x,y)=\text{the maximum number of edge-disjoint paths from $x$ to $y$}=\text{the minimum number of edges separating $x$ from $y$},
$$

 and define the **maxmaxflow** by

$$
\Lambda(G)=\max_{x\neq y}\lambda(x,y).
$$

**Maxmaxflow conjecture.** There exist universal constants $C(k)<\infty$ such that every chromatic root $z$ of any graph $G$ with $\Lambda(G)=k$ lies in the disc

$$
|z-1|\leq C(k).
$$

This weakens a bound in terms of the second-largest vertex degree. The paper notes that linear growth of $C(k)$ in $k$ is natural to expect, but does not prove the conjecture for arbitrary graphs.

record.title: Theta-graph extremal conjecture for chromatic roots at fixed corank
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph of corank $k$, and let

$$
\rho(G)=\max\{|z-1|:\pi(G,z)=0\}.
$$

For $k\geq 1$, write $\rho_k$ for the maximum of $\rho(G)$ over graphs of corank $k$, and let $\rho^{(2,k+1)}$ denote the corresponding value for the $(k+1)$-ary generalized theta graph $\Theta^{(2,k+1)}$.

**Fixed-corank theta extremal conjecture.** If $G\neq K_4$, then

$$
\rho(G)\leq \rho^{(2,k+1)}.
$$

In particular, for $k\geq 4$,

$$
\rho_k=\rho^{(2,k+1)}.
$$

The originally proposed statement without the exception $G=K_4$ is refuted: $K_4$ has corank $3$ and a chromatic root at $z=3$, whereas $\rho^{(2,4)}\approx 1.9636$. The corrected conjecture remains open in the supplied source.

record.title: The self-dual relaxed lattice equality conjecture
record.statement:
A **relaxed lattice** is a tempered distribution $g$ such that $g$ and its Fourier transform $\widehat{g}$ have the form

$$
\sum_{i \ge 0} a_i \delta_{r_i}
$$

where $a_i \ge 0$ for all $i$ (not all zero) and $0=r_0<r_1<r_2<\cdots$. It is **self-dual** when $\widehat{g}=g$.

**Self-dual relaxed lattice conjecture.** In every dimension, the largest possible value of $r_1$ among self-dual relaxed lattices equals the smallest value of $r$ possible in Theorem 3.2 of Cohn and Elkies.

This conjecture identifies the optimum of the rescaled self-dual relaxed-lattice problem with the optimum in the earlier dual-program bound for sphere packing. The supplied text does not state whether this equality has been proved or disproved.

record.title: The interval conjecture for degrees in quantum Schubert products
record.statement:
Let $X$ be the Grassmannian, and let $\sigma_{\lambda}$ and $\sigma_{\mu}$ be Schubert classes indexed by Young diagrams. Write $d_{\min}$ and $d_{\max}$ for the smallest and largest degrees of $q$ occurring with nonzero coefficient in the quantum product $\sigma_{\lambda}*\sigma_{\mu}$. **Interval conjecture.** The product $\sigma_{\lambda}*\sigma_{\mu}$ involves $q^d$ for every integer $d$ satisfying

$$
d\in [d_{\min},d_{\max}].
$$

The claim predicts that the degrees appearing in a quantum Schubert product form an interval, addressing the problem of determining precisely which powers of $q$ occur. The source gives computational evidence but no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

record.statement:
Let $(a(n))_{n\geq 1}$ be the EKG sequence defined by $a(1)=1$, $a(2)=2$, and, for $n\geq 3$, choosing the smallest unused natural number sharing a nontrivial common divisor with $a(n-1)$. **The EKG linear-bound conjecture.** The sequence satisfies

$$
a(n)\geq\frac{13}{28}n,
$$

with equality if and only if $n=28$, and

$$
a(n)\leq\frac{12}{7}n,
$$

with equality if and only if $n=7$. These sharper bounds are supported by numerical evidence, whereas the paper proves only substantially weaker linear bounds.

record.title: Sokal's half-plane conjecture for chromatic roots
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree, and let $P(G,t)$ be its chromatic polynomial. **Sokal's conjecture.**

$$

for every complex number $t$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{Re}(t)>\Delta(G).

This would strengthen the known zero-free exterior disc bound $|t|\geq C\Delta(G)$ and would be a half-plane analogue of Brooks's theorem. The source presents it as a possible extension and gives no resolution.

record.statement:

record.title: The Constant Conjecture for cohomology rings of Hilbert schemes
record.statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-projective surface. record.title: Higher syzygy degree bounds for finite-group invariants
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group in the nonmodular case acting on a finite-dimensional representation $V$. Let $\beta_G^i(V)$ denote the degree bound for the $i$-th syzygies of the invariant ring, and let $\tau_G(V)$ be the smallest integer $d$ such that every homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ lies in the ideal generated by all homogeneous invariants of positive degree. **Higher syzygy bound conjecture.** If $G$ is a finite group in the nonmodular case, then

$$
\beta_G^i(V)\leq (i+1)\tau_G(V)\leq (i+1)|G|.
$$

The preceding theorem proves the corresponding bound for the syzygy ideal, but the authors state that its proof does not seem to extend to higher syzygies. The conjecture proposes analogous bounds for all higher syzygies, using Fogarty's inequality $\tau_G(V)\leq |G|$.

record.statement:

record.title: Khashin's Mori-structure conjecture for the double space U
record.statement:
Let $U$ be the double space considered in the source, and let ${\mathcal S}$ denote the family of curves used there to construct the fibrations $V_l/\mathbb{P}^1$. **Khashin's conjecture.** The variety $U$ has exactly the following Mori structures: $U$ itself and $V_l/\mathbb{P}^1$ for every $l\in\mathcal S$, giving a two-dimensional family of different del Pezzo fibrations. record.title: The uniform distribution hypothesis for extremal B-star[g] sets
record.statement:
Let $R(g,n)$ denote the maximum size of a $B^{\ast}[g]$ set contained in $\{1,\dots,n\}$. A sequence $(S_n)_{n=1}^\infty$ of sets of positive integers **becomes uniformly distributed** if

$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{0\leq\alpha<\beta\leq1}\left|\frac{|S_n\cap[\alpha M_n,\beta M_n]|}{|S_n|}-(\beta-\alpha)\right|=0,
$$

where $M_n$ is the largest element of $S_n$. **Uniform distribution hypothesis.** Let $g\geq2$ be an integer. If $S_n\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ is a sequence of $B^{\ast}[g]$ sets with $|S_n|\sim R(g,n)$, then $(S_n)$ becomes uniformly distributed. The assertion generalizes the known result for $g=2$; its resolution for general $g$ is not supplied in the source.

record.title: The maximum-satisfiable-clauses scaling conjecture for random K-SAT
record.statement:
Let $N(n,m)$ be the maximum number of clauses that can be satisfied by one assignment of $n$ variables in a random K-SAT instance with $m$ clauses, and let $c^*_K$ be the threshold from the linear phase transition conjecture. **Maximum-SAT scaling conjecture.** Assuming the linear phase transition conjecture holds, for every $c>c^*_K$ the limit

record.title: Existence of strongly MDS convolutional codes with maximum distance profile
record.statement:
A convolutional code with parameters $(n,k,\delta)$ has length $n$, dimension $k$, and degree $\delta$. It is **strongly MDS** if it attains the strongly MDS distance bound, and it has a **maximum distance profile** if its column distances attain the corresponding upper bounds.

record.title: The MAX-SAT and SAT equivalence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $F(n,cn)$ be a uniformly random $k$-SAT formula with $n$ variables and $cn$ clauses, and let $f(n,cn)$ denote the expected maximum number of satisfiable clauses. For a fixed density $c$, consider the limiting expected satisfiable fraction and the limiting probability of satisfiability.

**MAX-SAT and SAT equivalence conjecture.** For any $c<0$,

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{f(n,cn)}{cn}=1
$$

if and only if

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\Pr\bigl(F(n,cn)\ \operatorname{is\ satisfiable}\bigr)=1.
$$

The conjecture is intended to formalize a connection between the MAX-SAT limiting function conjecture and the usual satisfiability threshold conjecture. The source provides no resolution status beyond presenting it as a conjecture.

record.title: Generalized Lehmer conjecture for abelian varieties
record.statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field $K$, and let ${\mathcal L}$ be a symmetric ample line bundle on $A$. For a point $P\in A(\overline{K})$, write $D=[K(P):K]$ and let $g_0(P)$ denote the dimension of the smallest algebraic subgroup of $A$ containing $P$.

**Generalized Lehmer conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c=c(A,K,\mathcal L)$ such that

$$
\widehat h(P)\geq cD^{-1/g_0(P)}
$$

for all nontorsion points $P\in A(\overline{K})$.

This is a height lower-bound problem for nontorsion points on abelian varieties, generalizing Lehmer-type conjectures for other algebraic groups. record.title: Subcritical largest-component asymptotics near the hypercube scaling window
record.statement:
Let $p_c(n)$ be the critical probability for the random subgraph of the $n$-cube, let $V=2^n$, and write

$$
p=p_c(n)-\epsilon n^{-1}.
$$

Assume $\epsilon\rightarrow0$ and $\epsilon e^{\delta n}\rightarrow\infty$ for every $\delta>0$. Let ${\mathcal C}_{\rm max}$ be the largest component. **Subcritical largest-component asymptotics conjecture.** Almost surely,

$$
|{\mathcal C}_{\rm max}|=\frac{2\log V}{\epsilon^2}[1+o(1)].
$$

If instead $\epsilon\rightarrow0$ and $\epsilon 2^{n/3}\rightarrow\infty$, then almost surely

$$
|{\mathcal C}_{\rm max}|=\Theta\left(\frac{2\log(\epsilon^3V)}{\epsilon^2}\right).
$$

These assertions extend the known subcritical estimates toward and beyond the scaling window, whose width is of order $V^{-1/3}$.

record.title: Chung's singular-value discrepancy conjecture for regular graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, write $e(G)$ for its number of edges and set

$$
\rho(G)=e(G)\binom{n}{2}^{-1}.
$$

For nonempty vertex subsets $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$, let

$$
disc_{2}(G)=\max_{X,Y\subseteq V(G),\,X\neq\varnothing,\,Y\neq\varnothing}\frac{\left|e(X,Y)-\rho(G)|X||Y|\right|}{\sqrt{|X||Y|}}.
$$

Let $\sigma_{2}(G)$ denote the second-largest singular value of the adjacency matrix of $G$. **Chung's conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every regular graph $G$,

$$
\sigma_{2}(G)<C\,disc_{2}(G).
$$

The conjecture asks for a direct comparison between spectral expansion and edge-distribution discrepancy in regular graphs. The source attributes it to Fan Chung; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
